class_name: 理由-因状況-イジョウハ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

glosses: now that; if it comes to
patterns.usage_note: からにゃ is a rough spoken squeeze of からには, at home in blunt male speech and fiction dialogue; the neutral forms are からには and the terser からは. It takes a fact the speaker has accepted and demands the resolve that ought to follow, so the second clause is typically a vow, an obligation, or an urging (〜つもりだ、〜べきだ、〜てほしい) rather than a neutral consequence. The front clause is normally something someone deliberately did or decided, which is why uncontrollable events like 雨が降るからには sound off; 以上は takes those comfortably.

examples.ruby: 引[ひ]き受[う]けたからにゃ、途中[とちゅう]で投[な]げ出[だ]すわけにはいかねえ。
examples.english: Now that I've taken it on, there's no way I'm dropping it halfway.

examples.ruby: 金[かね]を取[と]るからにゃ、半端[はんぱ]な仕事[しごと]はできねえ。
examples.english: If I'm charging money for it, I can't very well do a half-baked job.

examples.ruby: 約束[やくそく]しちまったからにゃ、意地[いじ]でも行[い]くしかねえ。
examples.english: I went and promised, so now I've got to go, come what may.

glosses: now that; since; as long as
patterns.usage_note: Marks a fact the speaker consciously acknowledges, and the clause that follows states the responsibility, resolve, or judgment that logically falls out of it. It is the flexible middle sibling: unlike からには, which wants a course of action someone chose, 以上は also accepts circumstances nobody chose (雨で中止になった以上は…), and unlike 上は it works in speech as easily as in writing. It also attaches to nouns and な-adjectives through である (学生である以上は).

examples.ruby: 親[おや]が反対[はんたい]している以上[いじょう]は、今[いま]は動[うご]けない。
examples.english: As long as my parents are against it, I can't make a move.

examples.ruby: 医者[いしゃ]に止[と]められた以上[いじょう]は、酒[さけ]は控[ひか]えるべきだ。
examples.english: Now that the doctor has told me to stop, I really ought to lay off the drink.

examples.ruby: 日本[にほん]で暮[く]らす以上[いじょう]は、地震[じしん]に備[そな]えておこう。
examples.english: If we're going to live in Japan, let's be ready for earthquakes.

glosses: seeing that (there is no turning back)
patterns.usage_note: The stiffest member of the trio, at home in speeches, editorials, and narration rather than conversation. The front clause names a commitment or a situation the speaker treats as already sealed — the fixed かくなる上は and the past-form こうなった上は are its signature openings — and the second clause states what one is now bound to do or the single course left, so it carries a note of burnt bridges that 以上は lacks; for a neutral or impersonal premise, and in ordinary speech, 以上は is the safer choice and has largely displaced 上は in modern prose. Its most idiomatic openings are かくなる上は and the past-form こうなった上は; with a non-past verb, take care, since 〜する上は is easily misread as the unrelated 〜する上で ("in the course of doing X").

examples.ruby: かくなる上[うえ]は、正面[しょうめん]から戦[たたか]うほかあるまい。
examples.english: It having come to this, there is nothing left but to fight them head-on.

examples.ruby: この道[みち]を選[えら]ぶ上[うえ]は、もう後戻[あともど]りはできない。
examples.english: Having chosen this road, there is no turning back now.

examples.ruby: 一国[いっこく]を率[ひき]いる上[うえ]は、私情[しじょう]を挟[はさ]む余地[よち]はない。
examples.english: In leading a nation, there is no room for personal feeling.
